title: Débit de filtration glomérulaire estimé cinétique (keGFR)
short_title: Débit de filtration glomérulaire estimé cinétique (keGFR)
formula:
Take two serum creatinine measurements (Cr~1~and Cr~2~), at two different time points (time~1~and time~2~).

Kinetic GFR, mL/min = (Cr~baseline~× CrCl / Cr~mean~) × [1 – (24 × (Cr~2~– Cr~1~)) / ((time~2~– time~1~) × 1.5)]

where variables are as follows:

| Variable* | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Cr baseline | Baseline creatinine, mg/dL |
| CrCl | Initial creatinine clearance, mL/min (by [MDRD GFR equation](nabda:calc.mdrd-gfr-equation\) ) |
| Cr mean | Average of Cr 1 and Cr 2 |
| time 2 - time 1 | Time between measured Cr 2 and Cr 1 , hrs |

*The second portion of the equation, i.e., [1 – (24 × (Cr~2~– Cr~1~)) / ((time~2~– time~1~) × 1.5)], is a multiplier limited to 0-1.

Note: formula assumes US units. For SI formula, see[O’Sullivan 2017](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/28396736).

how_to_use.why: Other equations estimating GFR ( [Cockcroft-Gault](nabda:calc.creatinine-clearance-cockcroft-gault-equation) , [MDRD](nabda:calc.mdrd-gfr-equation) ) have limited accuracy when creatinine is changing acutely.

next_steps.advice:
- While estimated GFR (by a validated equation) is adequate for most clinical scenarios, measured GFR is still considered the gold standard.
- Remember, eGFR is an estimate of kidney function, but is not included in the definition of AKI.

more_info:
Interprétation :

Un KeGFR de 30 mL/min a une spécificité de 90 % (sensibilité de 71 %) pour l'AKI, selon une petite étude rétrospective ([O'Sullivan 2017](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/28396736)).
medium_description: Estimates GFR chez les patients avec acutely changing creatinine.
